title: China-to-Saint Vincent and the Grenadines EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
target_market: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (SVGBS / VINLEC)
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Interoperability — IEC Type 2 / CCS2 vs GB/T
rows.target_requirement: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines UK / IEC electrical legacy and 50 Hz utility environment point toward IEC 62196 Type 2 for AC charging and CCS2 for DC fast charging, not the North American SAE J1772 / CCS1 direction. Type 2 and CCS2 become practical requirements where specified by SVGBS, VINLEC, a public tender, hotel operator, fleet owner, or charge-point operator. A pilot network should align with IEC 62196 from the start to avoid vehicle and spare-part fragmentation.
target_standards: IEC 62196-2 — Type 2 AC couplers
IEC 62196-3 — CCS2 DC and AC/DC vehicle couplers
IEC 61851-1 — conductive charging general requirements
IEC 61851-23 — DC EV supply equipment
rows.china_equivalent: China AC chargers use GB/T 20234.2 couplers and China DC chargers use GB/T 20234.3 couplers with GB/T 27930 communication. GB/T AC couplers differ from IEC Type 2 in connector gender and signaling, and GB/T DC couplers are physically and protocol-incompatible with CCS2. China-side GB/T connector evidence is not accepted as an IEC 62196 Type 2 / CCS2 substitute for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines projects.
rows.gap: A GB/T-only charger requires hardware redesign before Saint Vincent and the Grenadines deployment: coupler, cable assembly, locking, proximity and control-pilot circuits, DC communication stack, labels, temperature-rise evidence, and spare parts must be converted to IEC Type 2 / CCS2. Adapters should not be treated as a project-compliant solution. Confirm connector requirements before quoting because a small island market can be locked into the wrong ecosystem quickly.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where specified by SVGBS, VINLEC, tender, vehicle fleet, hotel owner, or charge-point operator; GB/T is physically incompatible with IEC Type 2 / CCS2
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 20234 applies to China domestic connector design and is not an IEC 62196 substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Saint Vincent and the Grenadines projects should be specified around IEC 62196 Type 2 for AC and CCS2 for DC. GB/T connectors are not compatible with that ecosystem, so conversion is a hardware and protocol redesign rather than a label change.

source.publisher: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Bureau of Standards (SVGBS)

rows.target_requirement: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines electricity supply is operated by St Vincent Electricity Services Ltd (VINLEC) under the regulatory oversight of the the energy-portfolio ministry. The island follows a 230 V single-phase / 400 V three-phase, 50 Hz utility system. Any grid-connected EV charger should be reviewed with VINLEC for service capacity, metering, load management, protection coordination, earthing, commissioning, and tariff or interconnection treatment, especially for hotel, fleet, airport, port, or public-site installations. Renewable-energy policy interest in geothermal and solar generation may support pilot charging projects, but it does not remove utility approval obligations.
target_standards: VINLEC utility connection and electrical service requirements
the energy-portfolio ministry electricity regulation
IEC 60038 — standard voltages, 230 / 400 V at 50 Hz
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic EV charger installations are designed around 220 V single-phase / 380 V three-phase, 50 Hz supply, GB/T 18487.1-2023 charging-system requirements, GB/T 20234 connectors, GB/T 27930 DC communication, and local grid-operator project acceptance. Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has the same frequency but a different nominal voltage at 230 / 400 V, so input voltage range, protective-device ratings, metering, thermal design, and power-quality behavior must be confirmed for VINLEC service conditions.
china_standards: China local grid operator project-acceptance requirements
rows.gap: Exporters must not treat 220 / 380 V China grid evidence as automatically Saint Vincent and the Grenadines-ready. Confirm 230 / 400 V input tolerance at 50 Hz, harmonic emissions, residual-current and overcurrent protection, metering, earthing, site load calculations, and VINLEC connection documentation. For tourism sites and renewable-energy pilots, confirm whether solar, storage, or load-management controls are needed to avoid local feeder constraints.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for grid-connected installations — VINLEC service approval and Ministry-overseen electricity requirements must be confirmed for the specific site
mandatory_status.cn: China local grid acceptance applies domestically and is not a VINLEC or the energy-portfolio ministry approval substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Saint Vincent and the Grenadines uses 230 / 400 V at 50 Hz, not China's 220 / 380 V baseline. A charger package needs VINLEC site review, 230 / 400 V input confirmation, IEC 61000 power-quality evidence, and load-management planning where feeder capacity is limited.

rows.requirement: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Market Access — SVGBS, the energy-portfolio ministry, VINLEC, and Frontier EV Demand
rows.target_requirement: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is an Eastern Caribbean OECS / CARICOM tourism economy with renewable-energy interest in geothermal and solar projects, but the EV market is essentially non-existent and should be framed honestly as a pilot-stage opportunity. SVGBS is the national standards body, the energy-portfolio ministry regulates electricity utilities, and VINLEC is the utility. Charger imports and deployments should be checked for SVGBS conformity documentation, customs classification, VINLEC connection approval, and site-owner requirements. Sea freight normally enters through Kingstown, so packaging, corrosion protection, spare parts, and service support should account for Caribbean logistics.
target_standards: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Bureau of Standards (SVGBS) standards and conformity assessment functions
the energy-portfolio ministry electricity utility regulation
VINLEC utility connection requirements
Kingstown sea-freight import route
OECS / CARICOM renewable-energy and tourism market context
rows.china_equivalent: China-market EV chargers are commonly documented against GB/T 18487.1-2023, GB/T 20234, GB/T 27930, China CCC where in scope, and domestic operator requirements. These documents can support a technical review, but they do not establish Saint Vincent and the Grenadines market access, IEC connector compatibility, SVGBS conformity, VINLEC connection approval, or service readiness for a small island tourism market.
rows.gap: Before shipment, confirm importer responsibility, HS code, SVGBS documentation expectations, VINLEC site approval, Ministry-overseen electricity treatment, IEC Type 2 / CCS2 connector scope, warranty spares, remote support, and coastal packaging via Kingstown. Commercially, avoid assuming a mass EV charging market; target pilots for hotels, rental fleets, public agencies, airport transfers, ports, and renewable-energy demonstration sites.

mandatory_status.target: Conditional — SVGBS conformity, customs, VINLEC connection approval, and Ministry-overseen electricity requirements depend on product scope and site; EV market demand is policy and project context, not a product-standard waiver
mandatory_status.cn: China CCC or GB/T evidence may support review but is not a Saint Vincent and the Grenadines market-access approval

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a frontier EV charger market. Treat sales as pilot projects requiring SVGBS, VINLEC, the energy-portfolio ministry, site-owner, logistics, and service planning; do not claim market readiness from China GB/T or CCC documents alone.

rows.requirement: OCPP, EMC, and Networked Charger Readiness
rows.target_requirement: For any Saint Vincent and the Grenadines public, hotel, airport, port, fleet, or renewable-energy pilot charger that is networked, OCPP back-office support should be specified for remote monitoring, billing, fault handling, access control, and load management. EMC and power-quality evidence should follow IEC 61000-family expectations so charger emissions do not create feeder or site interference, and so the charger remains resilient to island-grid disturbances, lightning, and switching transients.
target_standards: OCPP — Open Charge Point Protocol for networked charger back-office communication
IEC 61000 series — EMC, harmonics, immunity, and power-quality requirements
IEC 61851-24 — DC charger digital communication context
VINLEC site power-quality and connection requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China DC fast chargers commonly rely on GB/T 27930 communication between the off-board charger and the vehicle battery management system, while operator back-office functions may be proprietary or OCPP-based depending on the Chinese network. GB/T 27930 is not an OCPP back-office substitute and is not the CCS2 communication path expected for IEC deployments.
rows.gap: Confirm the OCPP version, SIM or Ethernet connectivity, remote diagnostics, local payment or access-control integration, cybersecurity controls, and load-management functions before deployment. For EMC, provide IEC 61000 test reports covering emissions, immunity, harmonics, flicker, surge, electrostatic discharge, and fast transients. GB/T-only DC communication and a China-only back office will not be enough for an IEC Type 2 / CCS2 Saint Vincent and the Grenadines pilot.

mandatory_status.target: Conditional — mandatory where required by the project owner, charge-point operator, utility connection review, public tender, payment system, or fleet-management specification
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 applies to China domestic DC charger communication and is not an OCPP or CCS2 interoperability substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Networked Saint Vincent and the Grenadines chargers should be specified with OCPP and IEC 61000 evidence from the start. A China-only GB/T 27930 communication stack does not solve back-office integration, CCS2 interoperability, or EMC acceptance.

rows.requirement: IEC 61851 Safety and Coastal Environmental Protection
rows.target_requirement: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Bureau of Standards (SVGBS) is the national standards body. For EV conductive charging equipment, the practical safety baseline should be IEC 61851-1 for general EVSE requirements and IEC 61851-23 for DC EV supply equipment, supported by enclosure, earthing, interlock, residual-current, overcurrent, over-temperature, isolation-monitoring, and emergency-stop evidence. Because Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a hurricane-exposed, humid, salt-mist coastal island, outdoor chargers also need corrosion-resistant enclosure materials, high ingress protection, UV resistance, wind and rain protection, surge protection, and thermal derating for tropical service.
target_standards: IEC 61851-1 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system, general requirements
IEC 61851-23 — DC electric vehicle supply equipment
IEC 60529 — IP Code for enclosure ingress protection
IEC 60068-2-52 — salt mist cyclic corrosion testing
SVGBS standards and conformity assessment requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China's comparable baseline is GB/T 18487.1-2023 for conductive charging system general requirements, with China-specific connectors and communication. GB/T safety reports may help engineering review but do not replace an IEC 61851 clause matrix, accredited IEC test evidence, or SVGBS-requested documentation for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
rows.gap: Prepare IEC 61851-1 and IEC 61851-23 evidence, IP and IK enclosure certificates, salt-mist or corrosion evidence for coastal service, tropical thermal derating, surge-protection ratings, installation instructions for hurricane-season anchoring and drainage, and maintenance instructions for tourism or fleet operators. GB/T 18487 evidence alone leaves connector, environmental, and IEC clause gaps.

mandatory_status.target: Project-critical and likely mandatory where SVGBS, VINLEC, importer, tender, insurer, or site owner requires IEC-family safety evidence; confirm exact SVGBS conformity route before shipment
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 18487 applies to China domestic design and is not direct IEC 61851 evidence

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat GB/T 18487 as a design input only. A Saint Vincent and the Grenadines-ready package should include IEC 61851 safety evidence plus coastal hurricane, salt-mist, ingress, surge, and tropical derating documentation.
